deep.reconstruction:
Setting (cote 154, 1983-84): Σ is a finite system (arrangement) of pseudo-lines in the projective plane. Grothendieck studies the 'positions relatives' (p.r.) of an additional pseudo-line D with respect to Σ, up to isotopy preserving Σ. In modern terms these are the single-element extensions of the rank-3 oriented matroid of Σ.

The positions are ordered by specialization and generalization. A position specializes when D is made to pass through more vertices of Σ. 'Stable' seems to mean generic: D passes through no vertex of Σ. 'Principal' seems to mean maximally special, a 0-cell that cannot be specialized further. 'Critique' and 'sous-critique' are notions defined on the surrounding pages (fuseaux, murs, balayages).

The page considers a non-principal D. S_D = D ∩ S is the set of multiple points (vertices) of Σ that D passes through, with |S_D| ≥ 2.

(1) Open question. Is every principal (critical) position passing through all of S_D a specialization of D?

For those D' = D'_δ that are specializations (because they are sub-critical for D), Grothendieck attaches a combinatorial datum:
- for each new vertex s ∈ S_{D'} \ S_D, an orientation arrow on the local 'pencil' Δ_s, i.e. which side D passes when it is pushed off s;
- a sense for the Δ_s with s ∈ S_D.
He claims that, for given δ, this system of arrows determines both δ and D. He starts writing the parameter space as a product ∏_{s∈S_{D'}\S_D} E_{D',s} of local choice sets. The pencil drawings at the top, with Δ1, Δ2, Δ3 through a vertex and dark-red arrows at the vertices, illustrate these local choices.

(2) Generalizations. The stable generalizations of D are the vertices of a ν-dimensional cell complex; the drawings and the counts identify it as a ν-cube.
- Its edges are the non-stable generalizations, those that still pass through exactly one vertex of S_D.
- Incidence between vertices and edges is the specialization relation.
- It is 'the product of the (main) diagonals of a polygon with 2ν sides', i.e. the zonotope that is a product of ν segments, with 2^ν vertices and ν·2^{ν-1} edges.
- The red sketch is a 3-cube drawn with its hexagonal projection; the black circle carries marked points (the 2ν-gon).

Justification, consistent with the mathematics: at each vertex s ∈ S_D, D runs from one sector to the opposite sector of the lines through s. Pushing D off s can only be done in two ways, around one side of s or the other. These local moves at distinct vertices are independent for pseudo-lines. So ν = |S_D|, and the poset of generalizations of D is the face poset of the ν-cube.

This serves the larger project on these pages: describing the cell structure of the space of relative positions (extension space), with fuseaux, critical positions and elementary sweeps (next page).
errors: Question (1) is left open on the page, and the restriction '(dans critiques)' suggests Grothendieck suspected it fails in general. A principal position through S_D may pass on different sides of other vertices of Σ between the points of S_D, and then it is not a specialization of D.

ν is never defined explicitly. From the cube picture it must be |S_D| (2^ν stable generalizations, one binary choice per vertex). 'Polygone à 2ν côtés' and 'produit des diagonales issues' are a loose description: the product of the ν long diagonals of a 2ν-gon, i.e. the ν-cube whose Petrie projection is that 2ν-gon.
The claim that the arrow system 'détermine δ et D' is asserted, not proved.

ideas.what: Positions relatives of a pseudo-line w.r.t. an arrangement Σ, ordered by specialization (passing through more vertices) and generalization
ideas.modern_name: single-element extensions of a rank-3 oriented matroid / extension space (poset of extensions under weak maps)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Las Vergnas (single-element extensions, 1978); Sturmfels–Ziegler, 'Extension spaces of oriented matroids' (1993); Mnëv–Ziegler
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme / Récoltes et Semailles as work on pseudo-line systems; no detailed published text known to me

ideas.what: The stable (generic) generalizations of a position through ν vertices are the vertices of a ν-cube; edges are generalizations still through one vertex; incidence is specialization. Equivalently, the upper interval of D in the extension poset is the face poset of a ν-cube.
ideas.modern_name: local cubical structure of the rank-3 extension space (independent local perturbations at each zero cocircuit)
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in rank-3 oriented-matroid extension theory (Sturmfels–Ziegler 1993; Bohne–Dress zonotopal tilings); not usually stated as a named result

ideas.what: Parametrizing specializations D'_δ of D by a product of local orientation choices ∏ E_{D',s} at the new vertices
ideas.modern_name: local sign-vector / cocircuit-signature description of extensions (zeros set to ± at cocircuits)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Las Vergnas; Bland–Las Vergnas; oriented matroid theory (Björner et al., 'Oriented Matroids', ch. 7)

ideas.what: Picturing the ν-cube via the zonogon / Petrie 2ν-gon (product of the long diagonals)
ideas.modern_name: cube as a zonotope; Petrie polygon projection

missed.claim: Independently of the oriented-matroid literature, Grothendieck identifies the local structure of the space of positions of a pseudo-line through ν vertices as a ν-cube. This shows the pseudo-line extension space is locally cubical, with cells of dimension up to the number of vertices passed through. That exceeds the dimension 2 available to straight lines, so it is a non-realizable phenomenon. It predates Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993) on extension spaces.
missed.quote: Les généralisations stables de D correspondent aux sommets d'un certain ensemble de dimension ν, dont les arêtes sont les généralisations non stables ... 2^ν sommets, ν2^{ν-1} arêtes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It belongs to the early history of extension spaces of oriented matroids (the extension space conjecture, topology of rank-3 extension spaces). It is an unknown independent precursor, but the statement itself is known or easy to specialists.

missed.claim: The question of whether every principal (critical) position through S_D is a specialization of D is left open.
missed.quote: Toute position relative principale (dans critiques) qui passe par S_D est-elle une spécialisation de D ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a question about the order structure (gradedness / upper intervals) of the extension poset. Specialists would likely settle it quickly, probably negatively in general.

deep.surprise_reason: These are sensible, correct structural observations on pseudo-line extension spaces made around 1983-84, independently of the oriented-matroid school. They are historically interesting as Grothendieck's late combinatorial work, but the cube structure is elementary and implicit in later literature.
transcription_corrections: 'un certain ensemble de dimension ν' — the drawings (cube sketch in red, 2^ν vertices, ν2^{ν-1} edges) indicate a ν-cube; 'ensemble' may be 'cube' or 'complexe' in the hand, uncertain.
'un sens pour premier Δ_0 (s∈S_D)' is more likely 'un sens pour [chacun des] Δ_s (s∈S_D)'.
'Il y a aussi le système des généralisations stables qui généralisent D' — 'stables' is an insertion above a struck-out word.
Bottom-left pencil sketch: a crossing of lines with an arrow, illustrating an orientation arrow on a local pencil Δ_s.
